summary: Intermittent cold-start latency spikes after aggressive idle-connection eviction in customer SDK leading to timeouts and retries
description: Issue summary: Glacier Analytics reports intermittent ~2-6s spikes in first-token latency for short-lived user requests from their web app. Spikes began after they upgraded to SDK v1.4.0 and changed client-side idle-connection eviction to aggressively close idle sockets (idle_evict_ms set to 1000). Impact: user-facing timeouts and increased visible retry counts, occasional 504s. Environment: Dedicated tenant in us-east region, traffic pattern is many short requests (avg token length small, high qps bursts).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use SDK v1.4.0 configured with connectionPool: {maxIdle: 2, idleEvictMs: 1000, maxSockets: 8}
2) Simulate bursty short requests (50-200ms request intervals) with a pool of ephemeral front-end workers.
3) Observe first-request/first-token latency distribution and retry counts over 10 minutes.
4) Reproduce with SDK v1.3.8 (previous) using default idleEvictMs=60000 to compare.
observed_behavior:
- Frequent first-token latency spikes: 1200ms - 6000ms
- Client-side logs show connection teardown and reestablish sequences immediately preceding spikes.
- Server-side access logs show a corresponding SYN/FIN patterns and short-lived TLS handshakes.
- Customer sees >15% of requests trigger SDK retries within burst windows, leading to apparent timeouts in the UI.
expected_behavior:
- Warm pooled connections reused with first-token latency ~80-150ms for these short requests.
- Low retry counts and no visible timeouts for typical burst traffic patterns.

investigation_notes:
- Repro locally with customer SDK config and our load generator: when idleEvictMs set to 1s, pool frequently drains between bursts and reconnects incur TLS + TCP overhead.
- Observed head-of-line effect: front-end worker tasks block waiting for a new connection to complete handshake while other in-flight requests queue behind application-level locks in SDK.
- SDK v1.4.0 introduced an aggressive idle evict implementation and a synchronous socket creation path for missing connections; combined with small maxIdle this amplifies cold-start penalty.
- Server-side metrics do not show serving-runtime slowness; CPU and GPU utilization normal. Network RTTs stable. Root cause points at client-side pool misconfiguration + SDK behavior change.
- Linked to customer-side thread model: ephemeral workers create spike of concurrent dial attempts leading to transient connection storms and a small fraction of requests experiencing serialized waits (per-thread lock contention in SDK client).
hypothesis: Aggressive idle eviction + low maxIdle causes frequent cold connection creation. SDK's synchronous connection creation path and a global mutex in the pool code serializes dial path, producing perceived high tail latency and retries. Not a serving-runtime regression.
root_cause: Client SDK configuration (idle_evict_ms=1000, maxIdle=2) combined with a synchronous dial path introduced in SDK v1.4.0 caused pooled sockets to be frequently torn down and re-created under bursty short-request workloads. Re-creation serialized inside the SDK led to head-of-line blocking and elevated first-token latency, triggering retries/timeouts at the application layer.
workaround:
- Immediate: revert to SDK v1.3.8 or set idleEvictMs >= 30000 and maxIdle >= 8 on customer side to keep sockets warm during bursts.
- Short-term: bump keepalive settings and enable SDK async dial flag (sdkOptions.asyncDial=true) to avoid synchronous blocking while connections are established.
- We recommended increasing read timeout client-side to avoid premature 504s while they test config changes.
resolution: In progress (customer applied recommended config change on 2026-03-11: idleEvictMs=45000, maxIdle=8). Observed immediate reduction in first-token spikes in our telemetry: 95th pct latency dropped from ~2.6s to ~160ms across sampled bursts. We opened SDK issue to make async dial default and to remove global lock in pool (PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/612). Patch to SDK landed in v1.4.2 and scheduled for canary release internal 2026-03-14.
follow_up_actions:
- Engineering: prioritize SDK pool fix (remove global mutex, default async dial) and ship in next minor (done in PR #612).
- Docs: add guidance for bursty/short-request workloads on connection pool tuning and defaults.
- SRE: add alert that correlates high client-side dial rates with elevated first-token latency for dedicated tenants.
- Customer success: check back with Glacier Analytics after canary rollout and mark ticket Resolved when 48 hours of stable telemetry confirmed.
